newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 31.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* America Online's proposal to pay up to $40 in refunds and credits to frustrated users of its service fails to appease all its customers.
* A Federal appeals court ruled that Motorola Inc and a sports statistics gathering company have the right to transmit scores from National Basketball Association games on pagers.
* South Korea's economy, still recovering from a month of worker strikes, is dealt another blow with the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co, the nation's second largest steel company.

* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan urged Congress to limit cost-of-living increases for Social Security and other Federal benefits and revived his call for the creation of an independent commission to set more accurate increases for inflation.

* The Bank of Boston said it would cancel the sale of its Fidelity Acceptance unit to Mercury Finance, a day after Mercury said accounting irregularites would force it to cut its reported profits for the last four years.
* An assistant commissioner at the Internal Revenue Service acknowledged that his agency spent $4 billion on its computer systems, but that the systems do not function well.
* The Dow industrials surged 83.12 points to close at 6,823.86.
* Conrail, CSX and Norfolk Southern meet today, but it is unlikely any substantive issues in the merger battle will be addressed because the talks are not protected by confidentiality agreements.
* Samsung Electronics said it will acquire the 51 percent of AST Research it does not already own.

* Shares of Gilead Sciences soared after the company said it will begin clinical trials of a drug to treat influenza, but Australia's Biota Holdings has a similar drug that could beat Gilead's to market. -- Market Place.
* Warner-Lambert shares rise 3-1/8 to 78 after the company gets FDA approval to market a new class of diabetes drug.
* America Online said it plans to lure more advertisers using the results of a Nielsen Media Research study showing homes that subscribe to its service watch less television.

* The Republican effort to eliminate and simplify federal regulations for businesses has stalled, and instead, Congress members are reaching for compromises that focus on using greater care in drafting new rules.
